title: Toyota Motor Corporation | Business and Management - EBSCO
content: Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi, Japan, is a leading global automobile manufacturer known for its diverse range of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and hybrids. It became the world's largest automaker in 2008 and remains a significant player in the automotive industry, employing over 370,000 individuals and producing more than 200 million vehicles since its inception. Toyota is recognized for pioneering the hybrid vehicle market with the introduction of the Prius in 1997, which was the first mass-produced hybrid automobile. Toyota's impact extends beyond manufacturing; it plays a significant role in the global economy and has strategic partnerships, such as its collaboration with Mazda. content: # History of Toyota Motor Corporation. ## Uploaded by. AI-enhanced title and description. Toyota Motor Corporation is a large Japanese automaker founded in 1937 by Kiichiro Toyoda. Toyota was originally a textiles company started by Sakichi Toyoda, who invented an automatic loom. Sakichi's invention impressed a British company, which bought the rights for £100,000. Sakichi gave the proceeds to his son Kiichiro to develop automotive technology, leading to Toyota's first car in 1936. title: August 28, 1937 - Toyota Motor Co is established
content: # August 28, 1937 – Toyota Motor Co is established. On this day in 1937 Toyota Motor Co., Ltd. is established. With encouragement from the Japanese Government due to a need for domestic vehicle production because of the war with China the company moved forward quickly with their development. The company produced its first engine in 1934 and the first car, a model A1 in May of 1935. The success of the company led to the formation of Toyota Motor Co, separate from the original Toyoda, which is now Toyota Group and still makes looms and sewing machines. The name was changed from Toyoda to Toyota because the number of strokes to write Toyota in Japanese characters (Kanji) is eight, a lucky number in East Asian culture, while Toyoda was nine strokes. When the US went to war with Korea the US government ordered 5,000 trucks from Toyota, putting them back in business for good.
